purpose: To produce a person who has been detained unlawfully before the court and secure their release
keyCases: ADM Jabalpur v Shivkant Shukla (1976), Rudul Sah v State of Bihar (1983)
notes: Can be filed by the detained person or any other person on their behalf. Not maintainable if detention is lawful or if the person is in custody of a competent court.

purpose: To command a public authority to perform a public duty that it has failed or refused to perform
availableAgainst: Public authorities, tribunals, courts, government bodies — NOT against private individuals or the President/Governor
keyCases: Chief Constable v R. Mann (2010), Comptroller & Auditor General v KS Jagannathan (1986)
notes: Requires the applicant to have made a prior demand for performance of duty. Cannot be issued against a private body unless it performs public functions.

purpose: To quash an order or decision of a lower court, tribunal, or quasi-judicial body that is illegal, exceeds jurisdiction, or violates natural justice
availableAgainst: Lower courts, tribunals, and quasi-judicial authorities
keyCases: Hari Vishnu Kamath v Ahmad Ishaque (1955), Syed Yakoob v KS Radhakrishnan (1964)
notes: Issued only when there is an error of law apparent on the face of the record. Cannot be used as an appeal remedy.

purpose: To prevent a lower court or tribunal from exceeding its jurisdiction or acting beyond its powers
availableAgainst: Lower courts, tribunals, and quasi-judicial bodies that have not yet passed a final order
keyCases: East India Commercial Co v Collector of Customs (1962), Calcutta Discount Co v ITO (1961)
notes: Issued before the order is passed (preventive), unlike Certiorari which is issued after the order is passed (curative).

purpose: To challenge the legality of a person's claim to a public office and remove them if their appointment is invalid
availableAgainst: A person holding a public office without lawful authority
keyCases: University of Mysore v Govinda Rao (1965), Jamalpur Arya Samaj Sabha v D. Rama (2004)
notes: Can be filed by any private person. The office must be a substantive public office of a permanent character created by statute.
